away.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
away.news: Vasilevskiy is coming off a solid 2025-26 season, winning his second Vezina Trophy, but he has been far from stellar to start the 2026-27 season. The 32-year-old Vasilevskiy struggled in his previous outing, allowing four goals on 26 shots (.846 SV%) in a 4-3 loss to the Winnipeg Jets. He has uncharacteristically allowed three or more goals in eight of 13 games this season (8-4-1). Still, Tampa Bay enters Wednesday's game as -126 road favourites against a Buffalo Sabres team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their last six games (4-2-0).

away.name: Joonas Korpisalo
away.news: Korpisalo recently made his season debut after returning from a lower-body injury and will return to the crease on Wednesday, suggesting the Rangers intend to rotate goalies for the time being. The 32-year-old Korpisalo saved 25 of 28 shots (.893 SV%) in his only outing, a 4-3 win over the Seattle Kraken. The Rangers enter Wednesday's game as -139 road favourites against a Calgary Flames team coming off a 4-3 win over the Philadelphia Flyers.

home.name: Devin Cooley
home.news: Dustin Wolf played while Cooley was recovering from a lower-body injury, but the Flames will return to leaning on Cooley. The 29-year-old Cooley was solid in his return to action on Sunday, saving 32 of 35 shots (.914 SV%) in a 4-3 overtime win over the Philadelphia Flyers. In his last six games (5-1-0), Cooley has a dazzling 1.86 GAA and .944 SV%. The Flames enter Wednesday's game as +128 home underdogs against a New York Rangers team that snapped its three-game winning streak on Monday with a 3-1 loss to the Edmonton Oilers.

home.name: Tristan Jarry
home.news: Jarry will start vs. Philadelphia on Wednesday.

home.name: Carter Hart
home.news: Hart will start vs. Utah on Wednesday.

home.name: Laurent Brossoit
home.news: Brossoit will start vs. Nashville on Wednesday.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov has had an up-and-down 2026-27 season. After one of the best stretches of his career at the NHL level, Askarov allowed 11 goals on 54 shots in two games (0-2-0), but rebounded in his most recent outing, saving 30 of 32 shots (.938 SV%) in a 3-2 shootout win over the New York Islanders. The 24-year-old goalie has allowed two or fewer goals in six of his last eight games (3-5-0). The Sharks enter Monday's outing as +124 home underdogs against a Pittsburgh Penguins team coming off a 5-2 loss to the Anaheim Ducks.
